description:
Sound Healing Music | Slow Surbahar | 1.5 Hours of Rest

If your shoulders are at your ears and your mind hasn't stopped since Monday — start here. The Surbahar's deep slow strings are designed for one thing: getting your nervous system to finally let go.

90 minutes of slow Surbahar music, the deepest of the Indian plucked string instruments. Tuned to a gentle healing frequency for the body to release stored tension.

🎵 What you'll hear:
- Surbahar — a deep, slow Indian string instrument with rich low resonance (think slowed-down sitar)
- Long sustained notes that match the rhythm of slow breathing
- A gentle frequency layer designed for the nervous system to soften
- Unbroken sound — no abrupt fades, no startling moments

⏱ Chapters
0:00   Settling in
12:00  Body softening
30:00  Nervous system releasing
60:00  Deep rest zone
80:00  Gentle return

🧠 How to use:
Press play. Lights low. Sit or lie down. Don't try to relax — the slow strings do the work. Phone face down.

⏱ Best for:
• End-of-day decompression
• Wired-but-tired evenings
• Pre-sleep wind-down
• Long rest sessions
• Mental exhaustion / burnout recovery

📺 Subscribe to Raga Focus for daily uploads:
- Sitar, Sarangi, Veena, Surbahar, Bansuri, Tanpura and other Indian instruments
- Music for anxiety, overthinking, sleep, stress, emotional release

— Raga Focus

thumbnail_prompt: Pichwai/Kangra miniature painting style, ornate gold-and-cream patterned border with subtle peacock and lotus motifs, aged warm parchment background, late-evening palette (deep amber with single warm oil lamp glow). Central figure: a serene woman in deep-burgundy-and-cream sari with gold accents seated cross-legged playing surbahar (recognizable by its large gourd resonator and long fretted neck — like a slower bigger sitar) in a quiet candle-lit room. Soft warm light through a window. A still water bowl or single drooping flower as visual rest-cue. Bold dark-teal serif overlay text reading 'FOR DRAINED MINDS' top-center, traditional Devanagari-influenced serif typography, high contrast for mobile readability. Aged warm cream parchment palette, contemplative restful mood, single composed scene, no clutter.
suno_prompt: Instrumental only, no vocals. Solo surbahar in raga Darbari Kanada, deep evening rest mood, slow contemplative tempo with sustained low resonant notes, no percussion, no tabla, no melodic lead instruments other than surbahar, 432Hz tuning, 65-70 BPM very slow tempo, deep meend slides and gamak ornamentation with long pauses, cinematic meditation production, deeply grounding, suitable for extended looping in post-production, begins immediately with surbahar already playing, no fade-in, no silent intro, full sonic presence from first note. deeply settled, like a body finally surrendering to rest

production_spec.loop_seam: 10s in / 30s out, Suno extend 3-4x → loop in post to fill 90 min
production_spec.notes: EMOTIONAL TAG ROTATION: clip 1: 'deeply settled, like a body finally surrendering to rest' · clip 2: 'deeply introspective, like breath held before release' · clip 3: 'gently hopeful, like tension quietly dissolving' · clips 4-7 cycle. Darbari Kanada tonic A or D. CRITICAL: Surbahar is the BIG version of sitar — deeper register, slower attack, more sustain. Suno may default to sitar — explicitly state 'surbahar', 'deep low register', 'slower than sitar', 'sustained long notes'. Do not allow tabla or percussion. Mix: Suno -3dB, Binaural -18dB, Tanpura drone layer -24dB (subtle drone behind Surbahar). 432Hz tuning canonical for healing-frequency audience. Direct replication of Apr 28 Deep Rest Surbahar formula (channel's #2 video, 19K views/26% AVD).
